name: Terminal timeout and lifecycle truth
ci_skip: needs an authenticated Claude CLI plus a provisioned nxd-desktop-supervisor runtime (EVAL_DESKTOP_SUPERVISOR_DIR, EVAL_DESKTOP_PYTHON, and EVAL_NXD_REPO_ROOT); run explicitly on a host with those components or via workflow_dispatch

checks.check: The first build receives the runner's structured client deadline error, including method and configured timeout, while the child server remains available.

A following inspect_run MCP call proves the durable run state and run identity. For an in-flight or failed run it also proves the diagnostic budget, active stage, retry count, and page/request count; for an already-published run it proves terminal publication without inventing diagnostic-only fields.

If the timed-out run was already published, the agent resumes it without issuing a same-workflow rebuild; otherwise a larger-budget or bounded-plan retry succeeds without a duplicate build and preserves the same fixture semantics.

Timeout, failed build, publication atomicity, cleanup, and resume-first versus rebuild remain distinguishable in structured evidence; cancellation is covered at the runner/process boundary because the current public MCP catalog exposes no cancellation operation.

Credentials and raw response bodies are absent from diagnostics; the required credential profile may remain only as a mode-0600, SENSITIVE/.gitignore-guarded runtime input; and the workflow leaves no live process or temporary state.
